title: Punch Miller and Percy Humphrey
summary: Played with Punch only in an advertisement; with Percy Humphrey many spot jobs before the 1949 recordings.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I like world rules and I like high society too. Do you like a lot of marches? No. No. I like Timberlaine. I like Timberlaine too. It's good. Several others are. I like Barry, no. I just can't think of them now. I've been in Gettysburg, you like that? Yeah. What about punch? Did you ever play with punch much? I never played with punch. I believe the only time I played with punch was on an advertisement. You know, like they used to advertise on a Sunday evening for a dance, at night, for a couple of hours. That's the only time I ever played with punch was an advertisement. That's when I had just started out. How about Percy Humphrey? How about Percy Humphrey? Was that with him? Oh yeah, I played with him a lot. When was that? Oh, that was before I went to Wake Reglin, owned up at Panna. I used to play a lot of spot jobs with Percy Humphrey.
I know Bill Russell told me that you wanted to record with Percy. What's that? Bill Russell had told me that you wanted to record with Percy. Way back.

That must have been about 44, 45. Yeah, about... Maybe 49. Maybe 49. I don't know. No, I don't think... No, 49, no. Must have been... Because he was with Joe Abraham Tillman, I think. I thought it was maybe the ones that were done with...
Herb Moran or somebody. That was 49. Well, I don't know.
I can't keep it straight now.
What did you play with Percy at the little clubs around town? Dances.
House dances, you know. Faternity dances. Things like that. Used to get...
